item.title: Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court has dealt with a series of cases over the past week. Among those appearing was Carl Crawford, 38, of Walton Highway, who admitted to stealing over £5,000 from an elderly woman with Alzheimer’s disease. He will be sentenced at Norwich Crown Court at a later date.
Meanwhile, 51-year-old Mark Pleasants of Terrington St Clement is due for sentencing on November 5 after admitting to possessing indecent images of children and extreme images depicting rape. Additionally, 32-year-old Olegs Belokurovs was fined £320 for shoplifting trainers from a King’s Lynn store, while 38-year-old Scott Manning received a six-week prison sentence for theft and criminal damage. Other hearings included charges of stalking, drug possession, and assault.

item.title: King’s Lynn Rotarians raise funds for Nepal flood victims
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn Rotarians raise funds for Nepal flood victims
Members of the King’s Lynn Priory Rotary Club have raised thousands of pounds to support those affected by recent flash floods in Nepal. Following the disaster, which was triggered by a collapsing glacier, club member John Harrison launched a fundraising drive to provide emergency shelter boxes. These kits contain essential supplies, including bedding, cooking equipment, and shelter for families who have lost their homes.
So far, the group has collected £3,000, enough to fund five shelter boxes. Additionally, the club has donated £500 to the Rotary District’s Nepal Disaster Appeal. Mr. Harrison, who previously served in the Royal Air Force, has a long-standing personal connection to the region through his past trekking and climbing expeditions.

item.description:

Senior doctors warn of workforce crisis at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
Senior medics at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn have warned that potential plans to downgrade A&E, intensive care, and maternity services could trigger a severe workforce crisis. In a leaked letter, consultants expressed profound concern that ongoing uncertainty is already damaging staff recruitment and retention.
The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group, which is reviewing clinical services, maintains that no decisions have been made regarding the future of these units. However, clinicians argue that a lack of clear refutation is undermining public confidence. The hospital serves a wide rural area, including parts of North Cambridgeshire and South Lincolnshire, leading to fears that any reduction in services would pose a significant risk to patient safety.

item.title: Wisbech man jailed for shoplifting offences
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech man jailed for shoplifting offences
A 44-year-old man from Wisbech has been sentenced to 13 months in prison for a series of shoplifting offences. Lee Thompson, of John F Kennedy Court, targeted the Tesco Express on Kirkgate Street three times between August 14 and 18. He also admitted to stealing from the Boots store in the Horsefair Shopping Centre back in May, alongside further offences committed in Norfolk.
Following his arrest by neighbourhood officers, Thompson appeared at Huntingdon Magistrates’ Court last Tuesday. The sentence includes the activation of previous suspended terms. In addition to his jail time, Thompson has been ordered to pay £99.99 in compensation. Police have thanked members of the public for reporting retail crime, noting that such information is vital for identifying offenders.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Inquest concludes into fatal Wisbech crash
An inquest has heard that 18-year-old Declan Berry was driving at 90mph before his car crashed into a river in Wisbech. The hearing at Cambridgeshire Coroners Court was told the vehicle, which was carrying five teenagers, hit a pothole on North Brink on March 18 before rolling into the water.
Three passengers escaped the submerged car with help from a local resident, but Mr Berry and another passenger died in the incident. Coroner Elizabeth Grey concluded that excessive speed was the primary cause of the collision, while noting that the poor condition of the road was a contributing factor. The court heard that the local council had previously received over 100 complaints regarding the state of the road.
